before.name: End of the Early Dynastic I Period, and the beginning of the Early Dynastic II Period in Mesopotamia

after.name: c. 2700 BC: One proposed Early Dynastic I–II boundary in Mesopotamia; dating varies

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The detailed ED article presents alternative boundaries 2750 or 2700 under middle chronology, a different short chronology, and contested applicability of ED II outside the Diyala. The overview also gives c.2650. This one-year slot is a periodization reference, not a verified political transition. Point/radius are broad southern Mesopotamian reference, not historical boundary. Existing ED I context overlaps at -2700 because the period dates are approximate.

before.name: Abandonment of the Mature Harappan settlement at Kalibangan in India due to the drying-up of the Ghaggar River

after.name: c. 2900–2600 BC: Early Harappan Kalibangan context; dates approximate

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The former row asserted Mature Harappan abandonment caused by river drying in -2700. Overview attributes it to c.2650; Kalibangan article itself contains inconsistent chronology and a dubious quotation, so neither exact date nor cause is asserted. It describes an earlier Kalibangan I occupation, its lead circa 2900 and end around 2600 followed by resettlement. The interval is a cautious contextual window, not proof of annual occupation, a precise founding or the date of final abandonment; 20 km is a game radius. NewsIndex can repeat the note yearly.

before.name: Supposed reign of the semi-legendary Sumerian king Gilgamesh

after.name: c. 2650 BC: Traditional Gilgamesh date; historicity and reign uncertain

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The overview gives c.2650 as a supposed reign; detailed biographies regard Gilgamesh as a legendary figure possibly based on an Uruk ruler, with historicity and dating not verified. This is a one-year reference slot to the overview, not proof of his life, reign, actions or presence in 2650. Regional coordinates and radius are not a verified exact residence.

before.name: Imhotep, vizier and architect of Djoser, constructs the Pyramid of Djoser, Egypt's earliest stone edifice, in Saqqara

after.name: c. 2667–2648 BC: Djoser step pyramid, one estimated construction period; dating varies

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The pyramid article gives one approximate date c.2667–2648; Djoser article gives several very different reign dates. The earlier -2700 slot asserted a construction year not supported by this source. Imhotep is a possible architect, not conclusively identified: ARCE notes no explicit contemporary attribution. Not Egypt’s earliest stone structure; the pyramid article calls it an early colossal stone building. Duration does not establish construction in every individual year; NewsIndex may repeat it.

before.name: c. 2700 BC: The beginning of statuary in Ancient Egypt, with shale and limestone statues of Khasekhemwy created in Nekhen

after.name: c. 2700 BC: Khasekhemwy royal statues from Hierakonpolis; date approximate

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The overview claims beginning of Egyptian statuary, an overbroad assertion; the Ashmolean-related statue description concerns early surviving royal examples, not all Egyptian sculpture. Two statues from Hierakonpolis date to the late Second Dynasty, but c.2700 is a reference estimate, not a verified creation year or verified manufacturing location. Coordinates refer to Hierakonpolis find context; 20 km game radius.

before.name: c. 2698 BC: Supposed beginning of the mythical reign of the legendary Yellow Emperor of China

after.name: c. 2698 BC: Traditional Yellow Emperor chronology; legend, not verified history

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The 2698 date is a traditional account of a legendary figure, not independently verified historical reign or an actual political event. Regional pin and 800 km radius are game references, not evidence of an ancient court or territory.

before.name: c. 2686–2613 BC: Third Dynasty of Egypt, consisting of the reigns of Djoser, Sekhemkhet, Sanakht (Nebka), Khaba and Huni

after.name: c. 2686–2613 BC: Third Dynasty of Egypt, one chronology; dating and sequence debated

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The dynasty article provides Shaw c.2686–2613 as one convention, and alternatives 2650–2575 and 2584–2520. Ruler order and identity are contested. Old row incorrectly used only -2613, the ending, and asserted political effect. Regional point/radius are game references; this context does not assert each ruler was active every year.
